title: Discovery of Non-peptide GLP-1 Positive Allosteric Modulators from Natural Products: Virtual Screening, Molecular Dynamics, ADMET Profiling, Repurposing and Chemical Scaffolds identification
content: Glucagon like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor is currently one of the most explored targets exploited for the management of diabetes and obesity, with many aspects of its mechanisms behind cardiovascular protection yet to be fully elucidated. Currently available therapy is limited to parenteral GLP-1 agonists with the demand for orally compatible formulations growing. Research dedicated towards the development of oral GLP-1 therapy and non-peptide ligands with broader clinical applications is crucial towards unveiling the full therapeutic capacity of this potent class of medicines. This study describes the virtual screening of a natural product database consisting of 695,133 compounds for positive GLP-1 allosteric modulation. The database, obtained from the Coconut website was filtered according to a set of physicochemical descriptors, and the quantitative estimation of drug likeness (QED) index. The resulting database which consisted of 158,523 compounds, was shape screened against the crystal ligand conformation and was filtered using a shape similarity (SS) score threshold of 0.3. This resulted in a final database of 26,325 compounds that was used for virtual screening against the GLP-1 allosteric site using three docking stages including high throughput virtual screening (HTVS), standard precision (SP), and extra precision (XP) docking. The results identified ten best hits with XP score ranging from -9.6 to -7.6 and MM-GBSA scores ranging from -50.8 to -32.4. The initial SP and XP shortlists were further subjected to docking pose filtration according to a set of criteria based on the crystal structure binding requirements. The resulting 58 hits were redocked using XP docking and their MM-GBSA were calculated and were found to be in the range of -7.4 to -3.7 and -52.77 to -13.02 for XP scores and MM-GBSA respectively. Molecular dynamics was performed on selected hits to verify binding stability within the GLP-1 allosteric binding pocket. The analysis of results identified hits from various natural products (NP) classes notably Sesquiterpenoids, Coumarins, and Phenylpropanoids, to whom attributed antidiabetic and anti-obesity effects have been previously reported. The results also pointed to unexpected compounds including β-lactam antibiotics including Valclavam, Cyclothiocurvularin B, Azidocillin, Ampicillin, Metampicillin, and Timocillin that may be evaluated in drug repurposing studies for off-target effects. The calculated ADMET properties for those hits revealed suitable profiles for further development in terms of bioavailability and toxicity. The structure analysis of the 68 hits revealed common structural scaffolds including peptidomimetics, lactams, coumarins, and sulfonamides with peptidomimetics being the most prominent especially in indole and coumarin cores.
